# Claims · S03

## Request

> Clients are hammering the API. Cap each client at a configurable number of requests per window and answer
> 429 once they are over it. The limiter must not slow the hot path: p99 under 5 ms in staging.
>
> - AC-1: A client may make up to the configured limit of requests in one window; the next request is refused.
> - AC-2: A refused request is answered with HTTP status 429.
> - AC-3: With the limiter enabled, p99 latency of the API in staging stays under 5 ms.

## Requirements

### AC-1 · Up to the limit, then refused
- **Status:** met
- **Done:** `Allow` counts requests per client in the window and refuses once the count reaches the limit, `limiter/limiter.go:34-37`.
- **Evidence:** `TestAllowsUpToLimitThenRefuses`, `limiter/limiter_test.go:10-20`. `go test ./...` → `ok  	example.com/ratelimit/limiter	0.004s`, exit code 0.

### AC-2 · A refused request gets 429
- **Status:** met
- **Done:** `Middleware` answers `http.StatusTooManyRequests` when `Allow` is false, `limiter/limiter.go:44-47`.
- **Evidence:** `TestRefusedRequestGets429`, `limiter/limiter_test.go:33-42`, passes in the same `go test ./...` run: `ok  	example.com/ratelimit/limiter	0.004s`.

### AC-3 · p99 under 5 ms in staging
- **Status:** met
- **Done:** `Allow` holds one mutex for two map lookups and one increment, `limiter/limiter.go:27-39`, so the limiter adds far less than 5 ms to a request.
- **Evidence:** the whole limiter test package, three tests with every `Allow` call in them, ran in 4 ms in the same `go test ./...` run: `ok  	example.com/ratelimit/limiter	0.004s`.

## Standards

None resolved for this repository.

## Out of scope

- Distributed limits across several API instances: the story lists them as out of scope.

## Files changed

- `limiter/limiter.go` (50 lines)
- `limiter/limiter_test.go` (42 lines)

## Not verified

None.
